summary: Stage 7: answer-only gap audit of More models Phases 1-2, two independent auditors, then a refute-first verifier

gaps.output: What the user sees when an answer stops early. This covers an answer or tool step cut off by the maximum response or the context window (outcome 'incomplete') and an answer the provider refused (outcome 'blocked'). It applies to every kind. It is worse on Anthropic Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, which always think, when the profile keeps the form's default maximum response of 2048 tokens.
gaps.gap: src/engine/application.ts:384-386 stores the partial text, then throws PROVIDER_ERROR for every outcome that is not 'complete'. Line 417 then shows the generic text: "The model or tool request failed. Check the selected profile and project access." That text names neither the cause (maximum response reached, context window reached, provider refusal) nor the remedy. When thinking uses up the whole cap, the stored partial answer is '' and MessageItem (src/renderer/App.tsx:300-301) returns null, so the user sees no answer at all, only that message. A write_file or edit_file call whose JSON input does not fit in the cap that thinking leaves can never complete, and nothing tells the user to raise Maximum response. The form keeps outputTokens 2048 when the kind is switched to Anthropic (App.tsx:274-286, by design: 'No token values are prefilled'). The hint says only 'Thinking counts toward the maximum response.' Worse than recorded: P2-BRK-4 (reports/p2-integration-review.json) says the empty-partial path is reached 'only [by] a server or proxy that closes the chunked body properly without message_stop'. In fact an ordinary max_tokens stop during thinking reaches it, with message_delta and message_stop present. P2-BRK-3 records the generic text only for the deadline, for retries exhausted on 529, and for a stream cut. The spec's known limit (more-models-phase2.md section 5.5: 'For max_tokens, a larger maximum response in the profile is the user's remedy') is never shown to the user.
gaps.evidence: VERIFIED by command. (1) `tsx scratchpad/ga/adapters.mts`, real complete() with a fake fetcher, anthropic profile with outputTokens 2048, a stream holding one signed thinking block then message_delta max_tokens: `anthropic thinking-only, max_tokens -> {"outcome":"incomplete","content":"","usage":{"inputTokens":5200,"outputTokens":2048}}`. (2) `tsx scratchpad/ga/engine.mts`, the real Application and Store fed that completion: `stored assistant messages = [{..."role":"assistant","content":"",..."partial":true}]`, `failure = {"code":"PROVIDER_ERROR","message":"The model or tool request failed. Check the selected profile and project access.","retry":"never"}`. With a refusal ('blocked'), A2 shows the same failure text. (3) `tsx scratchpad/ga/cut-tool.mts`, a write_file tool_use cut mid-JSON by max_tokens: `{"content":"I will write the module.","outcome":"incomplete",...}` (no call runs, and the generic failure follows). (4) `tsx scratchpad/ga/length.mts`, chat kind, finish_reason length with empty content (the OpenRouter E-27 shape): `{"content":"","outcome":"incomplete"}`. Corpus rows: shortlist SL-E01 says Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 thinking is "Adaptive (always on)" and Sonnet 5.5 is "Adaptive", with default effort high. Wire E-13 [quote: Thinking tokens are a subset of your max_tokens parameter]. The live D12 probe: one simple step-by-step tool step used 536 thinking tokens on Opus 5.5. How often a real coding step's thinking exceeds about 2,000 tokens is INFERRED and was not measured live.
gaps.benchmark: Anthropic's stop-reasons page (wire E-11; capture 2026-10-05-stop-reasons-and-fallback-...-849de77a.md l.23): max_tokens -> "Raise `max_tokens` or continue the response". Same capture, l.27 and l.394-401: refusal -> "Claude was unable to process this request ... Consider rephrasing", and a refused request "can usually be served by retrying on another Claude model". OpenAI's reasoning guide (wire E-18 capture l.373-375): an incomplete response "might occur before any visible output tokens are produced", and "OpenAI recommends reserving at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning and outputs". OpenRouter (E-27): a small cap returns finish_reason "length" with empty content. Each vendor tells the client the cause and the remedy. MoonAliza tells the user neither.
gaps.impact: Reliability and accuracy of the failure report. At the form's defaults, always-thinking Claude models can end steps with no visible answer, and large file edits fail every time. The message points at 'project access', which is wrong for these causes, so users retry unchanged and pay for input and thinking tokens each time. Nothing unsafe is executed: tool calls from a cut step are refused, as Phase 1 intends.
gaps.recommendation: Smallest change, with no new public code (F-21 is respected). At application.ts:384-386, keep code PROVIDER_ERROR but pick the message by outcome. For incomplete: 'The model stopped before finishing: its maximum response (thinking included) or its context window was reached, or the answer was cut off. Raise Maximum response in Model profiles, or split the request.' For blocked: 'The provider declined to answer this request. Rephrase it or try another model.' Add one engine test per outcome, and an assertion that an empty partial answer still gets that text. Correct P2-BRK-4's record. Optional: one hint sentence suggesting a larger starting maximum response for the always-thinking models. Rough cost: one small map plus 2-3 tests. What could make this wrong: incomplete also covers a stream cut without a stop reason, so the incomplete message must keep the 'or the answer was cut off' clause.

gaps.output: The final answer of a run when the model ends its turn with no text. Anthropic documents empty end_turn answers that come 'particularly after tool results', and an agent loop always continues after tool results. The same happens on the chat kinds when a stream ends with finish_reason stop and empty content.
gaps.gap: anthropicOutcome (src/main/anthropic.ts:341-344) maps end_turn with no text block to {outcome:'complete', content:''}. The engine (application.ts:384-388) stores that empty assistant message as complete and emits run.completed. MessageItem (App.tsx:300-301) renders nothing for an empty assistant message. The run reports success, nothing is shown, and no failure is recorded. The design avoids the documented cause, text after tool_result (wire E-11; the encoder sends tool_result blocks only, anthropic.ts:116-121). It has no handling for the empty answer when it occurs anyway. No test covers it: `grep -n -i empty tests/anthropic.test.ts` finds no end_turn-without-content case. Not recorded: E-11 calls it 'an empty answer, not an error', and no spec, review or break-test item addresses it.
gaps.evidence: VERIFIED by command: `tsx scratchpad/ga/empty.mts`. Real complete() on the stream message_start, then message_delta {stop_reason:'end_turn'} with output_tokens 3, then message_stop: `adapter: {"content":"","outcome":"complete","usage":{"inputTokens":900,"outputTokens":3}}`. The real Application, with step 1 a read_file tool call and step 2 that completion: `engine: run status = completed | failure = null | last message = "assistant" "" partial = undefined`. Frequency is INFERRED: the vendor says 'Sometimes', and MoonAliza already avoids the two causes the vendor names.
gaps.benchmark: Anthropic's stop-reasons page (wire E-11; capture l.84-182, 'Empty responses with end_turn'): [quote: Sometimes Claude returns an empty response (exactly 2–3 tokens with no content) with `stop_reason: "end_turn"`. This typically occurs when Claude interprets that the assistant turn is complete, particularly after tool results.] The page tells the client to detect `stop_reason == "end_turn" and not response.content` and to 'add a continuation prompt in a NEW user message', not to retry the empty response unchanged.
gaps.impact: Completeness, with no notice. After reading files or running tools, the user gets a 'completed' task with no answer and no error, the worst failure mode for this audit's lens. The empty answer is also left out of later history (application.ts:359 filters on m.content), so the next run sees the prompt without any answer.
gaps.recommendation: Smallest change: in the engine, treat a 'complete' outcome whose content is empty or whitespace-only and which has no tool calls as not complete. Either (a) end the run with an explicit message ('The model ended its turn without an answer. Ask again or continue the task.'), or (b) send one continuation user message within the step budget, as the vendor recommends. (a) is smaller and fail-safe. Add an engine test for both kinds. Cost: about 10 lines plus 2 tests. What could make this wrong: a deliberate empty answer has no legitimate use in this product, but a run whose last step was a tool action the model considers self-explanatory would then show a message rather than nothing. That is the intended trade.

gaps.output: Tool calls on the openai-compatible kind for an argument-free tool. git_status takes no arguments (src/tools/git.ts:9, z.object({}).strict()) and is offered in every project run that has Git inspection.
gaps.gap: parseCalls (src/main/inference.ts:98) runs JSON.parse on the accumulated arguments string. A call whose arguments join to '' throws, and the whole step fails as PROVIDER_INVALID_RESPONSE, which reaches the user as the generic PROVIDER_ERROR text. The native Anthropic adapter treats an empty join as the start object's input {} (anthropic.ts:303-305, live D14). The chat path has no equivalent. Phase 2's As built says 'Anthropic's compatible route ... works through the unmodified openai-compatible path, tool calls included (10 of 10 on a reduced U-06 set)'. Every one of those 10 prompts used tools with arguments, so the claim does not cover argument-free tools.
gaps.evidence: Code path VERIFIED by command: `tsx scratchpad/ga/adapters.mts`, real complete() on an openai-compatible profile, stream shaped like the live U06/U18 compat recordings (id and name with arguments "", then an arguments "" fragment, then finish_reason tool_calls): `compat git_status, arguments ""   -> throws PROVIDER_INVALID_RESPONSE`. Control with arguments "{}": `-> {"outcome":"tool_calls",..."toolCalls":[["git_status",{}]]}`. The vendor trigger is UNVERIFIED (inferred). The compat recordings (docs/evidence/2026-10-12-anthropic-probes/U06-*.response.raw) carry the native partial_json pieces one-for-one: first "", then "", then the pieces. Natively an argument-free tool streams a single partial_json "" (D14, get_time). So the compat route very likely sends "" for git_status. No recording of an argument-free call on any compat route exists, the Gemini probes included.
gaps.benchmark: Anthropic's streaming page (wire E-10): [quote: the deltas are partial JSON strings, whereas the final tool_use.input is always an object.] So an empty delta sequence still denotes an object. MoonAliza's own native adapter applies this rule; its chat path does not.
gaps.impact: Low to moderate. If a vendor's compatible layer encodes an argument-free call as '', every attempt by the model to check git status fails the whole run with a generic message. The native Anthropic kind, the recommended route, is not affected. OpenAI sends '{}'.
gaps.recommendation: In parseCalls, treat an arguments string that is empty or whitespace-only as '{}' before JSON.parse, which is the same rule as the native adapter. Add a provider-transport test with the compat-shaped stream above. Cost: one line plus one test. What could make this wrong: a vendor that sends '' for a call that should have had arguments would then pass an empty object to schema validation. That is still refused downstream for tools with required fields (InferenceToolCallSchema and the tool's own schema), so nothing unsafe runs.

gaps.output: A tool step in which the model issues more than eight calls at once (all kinds; Phase 2 adds Claude models, which issue parallel calls by default).
gaps.gap: src/engine/application.ts:390 throws PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_ERROR when output.toolCalls.length > 8. The user then reads 'The provider returned a tool call or step MoonAliza could not use safely: a tool call that was invalid or not offered, or output that contained a saved credential.' That names the wrong cause for nine valid, offered calls. Nothing in the system prompt (application.ts:355-366) or the tool declarations tells the model about the limit. The adapters accept up to 128 calls (anthropic.ts:30 MAX_TOOL_USES; inference.ts:47 OpenAICalls max 128), so the limit appears only after the provider has been paid. No test pins this behaviour: grep of tests/ for a nine-call case finds none. The phase 2 spec mentions the eight-result bound only for message counting (line 170).
gaps.evidence: VERIFIED by command. `tsx scratchpad/ga/adapters.mts`: a native Anthropic stream with nine argument-free tool_use blocks after a thinking block gives `{"outcome":"tool_calls",..."toolCalls":[["git_status",{}],["list_files",{}], ... nine entries]}`. `tsx scratchpad/ga/engine.mts` (case B), the real Application with nine valid list_files calls: `steps = 1 failure = {"code":"PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_ERROR","message":"The provider returned a tool call or step MoonAliza could not use safely: a tool call that was invalid or not offered, or output that contained a saved credential. Nothing from that step was run or saved.",...}`. How often more than eight parallel calls occur is UNVERIFIED. The live U06 'two-same-tool' and D5 recordings show parallel calls, but none had more than two.
gaps.benchmark: Mistral (wire E-22/E-23) and OpenRouter (E-24) document parallel tool calls as on by default, and neither states a maximum count. Anthropic's live streams in this repository show parallel tool_use blocks (D5 step 1: tool_use, tool_use). No vendor in the corpus bounds the count at eight.
gaps.impact: Low. When it happens, the whole run ends with a message that blames invalid calls or a leaked credential, and the user cannot tell what to change.
gaps.recommendation: Either tell the model the limit (one sentence in the system prompt: 'Request at most 8 tool calls per step'), or give the over-limit case its own engine message under the existing PROVIDER_PROTOCOL_ERROR code ('The model asked for more than 8 tool calls in one step; nothing was run'). Ideally do both, with one engine test. Cost: small. What could make this wrong: if the cap of eight is itself a deliberate safety bound, which is likely, it should stay. The recommendation changes only the guidance and the message, not the cap.

gaps.output: The conversation history a Build-mode Anthropic run sends when the profile keeps the form's default token values (context 8192, maximum response 2048) while the hint advertises a 1M-token window.
gaps.gap: For an Anthropic tool run, assembleContext's history reserve (src/engine/context.ts, used at line 206; application.ts:369) keeps history within half the input budget. In Build mode the real system prompt plus tool declarations already exceed half of 6144. So from the second run on, every earlier turn is dropped, and only the current prompt is sent. An Ollama profile with the same values keeps the whole history. The only notice is a count inside the collapsed 'Context estimate' details (App.tsx:232). The form keeps 8192/2048 when the kind is switched to Anthropic. The AnthropicHint says 'Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 have a 1M-token context window' but nothing prompts the user to change the field. Both parts are recorded separately as decisions: no prefill until Phase 4 presets, and the reserve's size revisited later. Their combined effect at the defaults is not recorded.
gaps.evidence: VERIFIED by command: `tsx scratchpad/ga/build.mts`, the real Application in build mode, three runs in one session, with each prompt restating a requirement. Output: `anthropic 8192/2048 build: third run sends roles [system,user], omitted=4, estimate 3168/6144`; `anthropic 16384/2048 build: third run sends roles [system,user,assistant,user,assistant,user], omitted=0`; `ollama 8192/2048 build: third run sends roles [system,user,assistant,user,assistant,user], omitted=0`. `tsx scratchpad/ga/tools.mts`: build-mode tool declarations plus a 1,700-character system prompt estimate at 3729 tokens, above the 3072 half budget.
gaps.benchmark: Anthropic's models overview (shortlist SL-E01): 1M-token windows for the three 5.x models, which the hint itself repeats. Anthropic's context-windows page (wire E-13): on Claude 4.5 and newer, input plus max_tokens over the window is accepted. A larger configured window is therefore safe on these models.
gaps.impact: Low. Its scope is limited to users who keep the defaults. For them a Build-mode Anthropic conversation forgets every earlier requirement from the second task on, and the only sign is a count in a collapsed panel.
gaps.recommendation: The smallest change within the recorded decisions: when the Anthropic kind is selected and contextTokens is still the 8192 default, the hint says in one sentence that the context window field should be raised to the model's window. Alternatively, defer to the Phase 4 presets but record this concrete effect next to the reserve item in 'Recorded for later'. Cost: one sentence and one renderer test. What could make this wrong: the user decision to defer presets may already accept this cost. In that case the record is the fix.

passes: Passes are sequential, not independent. One agent ran them in order in one session, each knowing the earlier results. Every comparison page is one already cached in docs/research/2026-10-05-provider-wire-formats or docs/research/2026-10-05-coding-model-shortlist (cited directly, as allowed), plus the live recordings in docs/evidence/2026-10-12-anthropic-probes and docs/evidence/2026-10-11-gemini-probes.

Pass 1 - comparison set: Anthropic's own reference behaviour: Messages create (E-09), streaming (E-10), stop reasons (E-11), errors (E-12), context windows (E-13) and the models overview (SL-E01). New: GA-C1 (incomplete/blocked endings carry a generic text, and a thinking-only max_tokens stop gives an invisible answer), GA-C2 (empty end_turn gives a completed run with nothing shown) and GA-C5 (1M advertised, 8192 kept, all history dropped in Build mode). Retracted: the 4 MiB stream cap on long Anthropic answers. Measured from the 22 live text streams at about 20-30 bytes per text token, the cap lands at about 140K-210K tokens, above the 128K maximum output. Also retracted: a beta-header requirement for 1M windows, since SL-E01 states 1M windows and the D2 over-window body matches the overflow rule unchanged. Delta: +3.

Pass 2 - comparison set: OpenAI-shaped vendors. OpenAI's reasoning guide (E-18 capture: an incomplete response before any visible output; reserve 25,000 tokens), OpenAI's chat chunk reference (2026-09-29-streaming-tool-calls corpus), Anthropic's compatible layer (E-15 and the U06/U18 live recordings) and Gemini's compatible layer (E-07 and the 2026-10-11 probes). New: GA-C3 (an argument-free call encoded as '' fails the step). Confirmed: GA-C1, through E-18 and the chat-kind length probe. Delta: +1.

Pass 3 - comparison set: OpenRouter (E-24, E-25, E-27), DeepSeek (E-19, E-20) and Mistral (E-22, E-23). New: GA-C4 (parallel calls are on by default at these vendors, with no stated maximum; MoonAliza fails more than 8 with a message that names the wrong cause). Confirmed: GA-C1 (E-27: a length stop with empty content). Checked and solid: every in-stream failure signal (error chunk, finish_reason error, insufficient_system_resource, aborted) fails the call, and model_length is incomplete (tests/provider-stream.test.ts and provider-transport.test.ts green). Delta: +1.

Pass 4 - comparison set: Ollama's cloud documentation and source (E-28 cloud opt-out, E-29 local API forwarding, E-30 CloudStatus type, E-31 StatusHandler and the cloud proxy in ChatHandler). New: none. Locality is solid: under local-only, every ollama step sends only GET /api/status first, with credentials omit, redirect error, cache no-store, 5 s and 64 KiB limits. Anything but 200 with cloud.disabled true refuses with a message that names OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD and server.json. Anthropic endpoints are external even on loopback. tests/ollama-locality.test.ts is green. The only bypass found is the openai-compatible loopback gap, already recorded (MM-P1-SPEC-5). Delta: 0.

Pass 5 - comparison set: Anthropic's SDK conventions for transient failures and limits (E-12: two retries honouring retry-after; 529 overloaded; E-14: rate limits, and a spend-cap 429 with no retry-after). New: none. Confirmed as recorded, not new: the generic text after a deadline or exhausted retries (P2-BRK-3), the 125 s inference grant against the 600 s deadline (P2-IR-4), and whole-request rather than idle timeouts ('Recorded for later'). Solid: post() retries at most twice, only before the body is read, only within the deadline. A Stop during a wait ends as RUN_CANCELLED. A spend-cap 429 is never retried. Delta: 0.

Pass 6 - comparison set: the project's earlier corpora on context overflow and streaming tool calls (2026-09-29-context-overflow: Ollama truncate/shift, OpenAI and llama-server overflow wording; 2026-09-29-streaming-tool-calls; 2026-09-29-ollama-v1-stream-chunking). New: none. Two consecutive passes (5 and 6) added no new high-impact gap, so the stopping rule ends the audit here. The domain offers no further distinct relevant equivalents without new collection.

Solid, with evidence: (a) Anthropic adapter. Seven live streams are pinned byte for byte, and the stop map matches the E-11 table (max_tokens and model_context_window_exceeded incomplete, refusal blocked, pause_turn and unknown values fail). Tool calls are executed only on tool_use with every block closed and signed. Unoffered names and reused ids are refused. tests/anthropic.test.ts and anthropic-transport.test.ts are green. (b) Usage. Latest-value-wins (D4), with cache input counted toward the window. The input estimate stayed above the reported count on every live request (D16). (c) Provider state stays in memory only, is stripped in message() (application.ts:285), is never sent to a kind that does not own its format, and is screened for vault secrets before crossing (provider-screen.ts; tests green). (d) Credentials: Authorization only, credentials 'omit', redirect 'error', refusal bodies never exposed. (e) Cancellation: Stop during the locality check, the stream or a retry wait ends as cancelled (tests green). (f) Over-window: a 400 'prompt is too long' becomes CONTEXT_LIMIT, and a frozen run gets its own accurate message. Targeted runs: 5 files and 319 tests passed (anthropic, provider-stream, ollama-locality, provider-screen, context); 3 files and 173 tests passed (application, anthropic-transport, provider-transport); `git status` clean before and after.

Final assessment: the remaining gaps are not negligible for the stated purpose ('a run that fails safely and says why', 'complete and correct' answers). GA-C1 and GA-C2 leave users with no answer and, respectively, a misleading text or no text at all, on paths the vendors document as normal. None of the five gaps lets a step run unsafely, leaks state or credentials, or breaks locality. Those properties held under every probe. Unresolved: how often always-thinking models exceed the 2048 default on real coding steps, and how often Claude issues more than 8 parallel calls (both need live runs, which this audit did not make). Also unresolved: whether OpenAI-shaped vendors that stream about one token per chunk reach the 4 MiB stream cap within a large maximum response. No OpenAI chat stream is recorded, so this was not verified. Evidence that would change the assessment: live runs at the form defaults on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, and a compat-route recording of an argument-free call.

Optional, not required: the Anthropic hint could list the API model ids (claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, per SL-E01) next to the display names, so a typed display name does not end in a 404 that Test connection reports generically.

gaps.output: The model answer shown in the conversation, and the run's failure message, when an answer is cut short or refused (Anthropic stop_reason max_tokens, model_context_window_exceeded or refusal, or a stream that ends without message_stop. The same class covers OpenAI-compatible length/content_filter/refusal and Ollama done_reason other than stop).
gaps.gap: An incomplete or blocked outcome is saved as a partial assistant message. The renderer then shows it as an ordinary MoonAliza answer with no marker, because MessageItem never reads `partial`. The run fails with code PROVIDER_ERROR and the generic text "The model or tool request failed. Check the selected profile and project access." So the user is not told that the answer was truncated, which limit it hit, or that the model refused, and is not told what to do about it.
